slots.hypothesis: This is core A's second and last E slot. Core A is the 50-day skew of the stock's daily realized variance: did the last 50 days contain an isolated, extreme volatility-burst day? Last round's R ruled out five confounds: zero-volume minutes, nominal price, squared vs not, needing the raw right tail (log and Bowley skew both kill it), and up/down asymmetry. Last round's E grew core x same-day turnover (1.41). Both centerings are necessary, and the reward's linear neutralization cannot remove a product. The family control now holds core x Amt and the core itself. So the 16 seeds use conditioning variables last round never tried, chosen from friction and mispricing proxies (Muller-Schmickler; Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan): turnover (today and 20-day), abnormal volume (madz60), size (cs_robust_z, so it avoids the periphery already seen with ListAge), 20-day and 5-day return, MAX, volatility level, 20-day overnight drift, and the position of the latest burst. They also cross core A with the seed's own uncontrolled axes (timing gap, overnight skew, minute kurtosis), and add new forms: a V-shape abs, a V-shape x Amt, and a cs_last_low40 one-sided screen. The screen uses 40% because local simulation gave rank correlation with the core of 0.67 at a 20% screen and 0.82 at 10%. No cs_bucket_rank seeds and no price, age or zero-ratio conditioners, since all of those lost last round.

The overnight vs intraday split, plus the interaction mechanism moved onto the seed's other two uncontrolled axes. Last round's single N hit was the overnight skew (1.16, sign +1). It needs the overnight gap (without ts_delay it falls to -1.02), while close-to-close and intraday skew both scored <= 0.12, and none of the five controls contains anything overnight. The 15 seeds cover: the overnight/intraday tug of war (50-day correlation, lagged correlation, 20-day drifts and their difference, overnight skew minus intraday skew); the overnight share of total volatility and whether gaps come with volume; up-gap and down-gap tails taken separately; the drift in the first minute after the opening call auction; centered-rank products of overnight skew, overnight drift and the core-B timing gap with Amt; the last-30-minute share of turnover vs the share of |r|; and turnover-weighted vs clock volatility.
